brands.name: Psillakis Surfboards
brands.short_description: Hand-shaped custom surfboards by Mike Psillakis in Brookvale, Sydney — performance shortboards, hybrids, twins, and guns from a shaper mentored by Simon Anderson since 1989.

models.name: 80s Twin
models.description: The 80s Twin was the mainstay before the thruster was developed and then superseded the twin fin design. Now the twin fin has re-emerged with better fin positioning and rockers. This has brought some spice back into the design with great feedback. Order the 80s Twin 1 inch shorter than your current shortboard.

models.name: Bootboard
models.description: Wide point set forward. Volume pushed towards the nose, relaxed entry rocker, with low rails, foiled tail with Vee double concave entry for breaking up the water into a slight single concave to Vee double concave tail for when the waves are ON.

models.name: BumbleBee Round
models.description: The Bumblebee round is a natural progression from the original Bumblebee, to be surfed in a variety of conditions but with the demand of more volume and ease of paddle power.This model has an extra 3/4 inch in width and 1/8 thicker than the original Bumblebee swallow and the rails are mid to low/soft for rail engagement to accommodate for the wider template. The bottom contours have a rolled V entry into a very slight V double concave tail with a low rocker to suit a wide variety of conditions. models.name: BumbleBee Swallow
models.description: The BumbleBee is not a fish! It’s designed as an alternative board ridden in a variety of waves. The plan shape is unique with a snub nose, wide point forward of centre and a straighter curve in the planshape leading into the swallow. This board has been tested in average beach break surf to more serious waves like in Indo with amazing results. Originally designed as a quad, but can be ridden as a thruster given the 5 fin option.Best way to describe The BumbleBee is, if you had no choice but to take one board with you on a trip, this would be it.Ride this board shorter than your normal board. models.name: Contemporary Gun
models.description: Classic contemporary gun for the seasoned surfer.Whether in Hawaii, Indonesia or at your home break and the swell is on. Some minor changes with a slightly wider outline for better paddling and maneuverability the contemporary gun is your timeless gun for waves in the range of double to triple overhead. Don't be caught under gunned.

models.name: Deep Ocean Guns
models.description: This board is only for the experienced and not for the faint hearted.Featuring high volume for paddle power, with super foiled tail for control and sensitivity. A complexed Vee, concave bottom contours for control and speed in critical sections.Working with big wave surfers giving me constant feedback has resulted in a highly refined gun thatwill give you the confidence to take on any big wave zone that you can handle.Custom ordered to specific wave types

models.name: Evil Eye

From 55″ to 70″ this board suits anyone looking to draw different lines on a wave.

models.name: Fly Fish
models.description: The Flyfish has maximum plan shape curve for assisted ease of turning and to fit in tighter areas of a wave face while the lower rocker for picking up speed and sustaining it through flatter sections. models.name: Flyer Twin Rounded Pin
models.description: Latest addition to the Psillakis surfboard collection is the Flyer twin rounded pin. Developed with a good friend Damian "Taco" Warr, this performance Twin fin is an all round design that replaces a conventional thruster for those wanting an alternative feel. The rocker has a slightly lower entry with a medium tail rocker. Single concave from nose to tail with low rails for sensitivity and control. Twin fins have less drag than thrusters, because there are only two fins. The key to the Twin fin is knowing where to place them on the board so you can achieve control and drive. Also available in EPS EPOXY

models.name: High Performance Midlength
models.description: The High Performance midlength is a new addition to 2023. Without sacrificing too much paddle power, the high performance midlength has more rocker and lower rails. Making the midlength surf more top to bottom with a quicker response. Also available in EPS EPOXY

models.name: Lazy Susan
models.description: Features a clean classic outline, foiled down rails with a rolled Vee tri plan hull bottom. The Lazy Susan brings a smooth classic feel to your repertoire, without too much effort. To be ridden as a quad or single with side bites. Pull the Lazy Susan out when you're not feeling like riding your shortboard. Best in 3 to 6 feet.

models.name: Mid Length
models.description: So you want to be a little more relaxed without losing performance. My midlengths are still built with performance in mind. The midlength has the length and wide to accommodate a more relaxed approach, but the abundance of outline curve and rocker helps this design fit into the "curl" of the wave better. Can also be customised to suit you local spot.

models.name: Mini Ninja
models.description: I wanted to create a shortboard that is progressive in below average conditions.The Mini Ninja has a low rocker (MPD rocker) for more drive and paddle power. It has a short board mid rail for quick response and hold in steep sections. Its kind of a fish in disguise, so you can cheat on this board. This board is fun but progressive. models.name: Miss Curvaceous
models.description: The Miss Curvaceous is one of the most exciting boards I have designed. The first response from surfers is that this board has an “electric, sparky” feel, thanks to the deepish single concave leading into the fin area. This board is designed to be surfed tight in the pocket of the wave. Extremely high performance board, but very user friendly.The rails are forgiving and it has a slightly different balance in the plan shape giving it a freer nose feel. Slightly wider tail than the gypsy and hipster models to accommodate the extra tail rocker. This board has a unique rocker (MPB rocker) /concave combination which I believe will make this board one my best performance shortboards. Who should ride this board? If you are of average to advanced ability and are looking to take your surfing to the next level in waist to a little over head high waves. Ride The Mode as your “go to” all round short board from 2 to 6ft waves. models.name: The Galaga
models.description: The 80s surfboard evolution saw the birth of the thruster. This bought in the no nose template and wide point behind centre. With flat decks, forward volumes and foiled tail still the norm of the era, wave catch abilities was no issue. Vee bottoms were the standard. This bought smooth rail to rail transition and a larger sweet spot. Tail rockers were generally flater at the time. This was great for a relaxed less effort for speed feel. The Galaga model brings back these design qualities but with slight modern refinements with rockers and volumes.Loud and proud sprays with checkers and bright colours are encouraged. Also available in EPS EPOXY

models.name: The Gargamel
models.description: Packing plenty of foam in this gun is what the Gargamel is about. Rolled entry with a tri plane hull with a deep Vee tail, making the Gargamel somewhat very nimble for a high volume gun. This model is made for those who want to move around in a double overhead lineup with ease, yet having enough performance for a quick responsive feel.

models.name: The Gypsy

Single concave through the midpoint to a deeper double inside a single concave through the fin area.The rails are medium soft. These designs features allow the Gypsy to be surfed in a variety of conditions. The Gypsy feels at home on any beach, reef break in small to medium size surf. models.name: The Super Greek Freak
models.description: This Model was born from my brother Mercury's request for a high performance shortboard to have some 80s influence thrown in, with some ease and fun to it. Mercury's quote for the Super Greek Freak was, "party at the front, business at the back". Meaning that the nose to wide point is slightly wider for added stability. The nose rocker is lower for ease of paddle and glide onto waves. And the tail end has slightly more rocker for getting tight into the lip. The deck is flatter, bringing most of the volume out to the rail, with a steep tapered low crisp rail. This gives the board maximum buoyancy and hold at the tip of the rail. The nose has a slight beak for added forward volume which adds to more ease and glide. This board was designed to give maximum enjoyment without the sacrifice of performance.
